decision: A 67.5 ERA after 2/3 inning says almost nothing; Skenes remains elite, though the career-ERA deficit takes many starts to erase.
ev_analysis: Forecast his next starts at his career per-start mean (1.97 ERA); the one start barely moves that mean.
why: The career mean lands on 'he is still elite', but the recovery arithmetic (how long to forget) is a sequence the analyst cannot pose.

decision: Alonso is more likely than not (60%) to finish 2026 under .250; the Mets were probably right to let him go.
ev_analysis: Forecast his 2026 BA as his 2023-25 mean, .245, i.e. under .250.
why: The point estimate points the same way but turns a 6-in-10 chance into a certainty.

decision: No mock draft can be perfect, yet the best analysts (~12 of 32) are far better than chance (~1).
ev_analysis: Mean exact matches for best analysts (12.0) vs Kiper (~4) as next year's expected hits.
why: Group means give the expected 12 of 32, but the chance baseline and the impossibility of a perfect board need combinatorics the analyst lacks.

decision: Brace for Soto to miss 10+ games (54%), though a short absence remains possible (40%).
ev_analysis: Mean games missed for calf tightness in the prior categories, about 12.6, i.e. 'two weeks'.
why: The mean says 'about two weeks', matching the brace-for-it call, but hides the skew and the 40% day-to-day hope.

decision: The EO shrinks the portal by about a third; portal-dependent programs lose, HS-first programs gain.
ev_analysis: Mean share of repeat transfers (28%) as the floor of the cut, and mean net portal flow by program type (-6 vs +7).
why: Group means reproduce who depends on the portal and part of the cut, but the deterrence share is an assumption, not a mean, so the 35-40% is stated without basis.

decision: Transfer limits make Indiana-style instant rebuilds nearly impossible while protecting programs already built.
ev_analysis: Mean portal intake by program type, cut by the 28% repeat-transfer share.
why: The group-mean arithmetic gets the direction (mid-tier loses most), but the projection rests on assumed deterrence the analyst would state as fact.

decision: The EO partly restores blue-blood dominance (to roughly 78-83% of titles) and its enforcement lever is dangerously oversized.
ev_analysis: Blue-blood title share by era: pre-portal 85% vs portal-era 70%; forecast under EO = pre-portal mean, 85%.
why: Using the old-era group mean as the forecast predicts full reversion, where the issue's decision is partial restoration.

decision: At 7-14 the Mets' season is bad but not over: projected about 80-82, interval 70-89.
ev_analysis: Mean final record of past teams that started 7-14, which ignores the 83-win preseason projection.
why: The natural group (bad starters) pulls the forecast well below the posterior and, with no interval, drops the 'not final' message.

decision: Early-season numbers are mostly noise until they pass stabilization thresholds (BA ~910 AB, K% ~60 PA).
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Stabilization is a reliability (split-half correlation) question; a group mean cannot say when a player's own number starts to count.

decision: Bad-start teams make the playoffs about 11% of the time, and P(A|B) is not P(B|A).
ev_analysis: Mean of a 0/1 playoff indicator among teams starting at or below .400 (about .11).
why: The decision is a group base rate, which the group mean delivers directly.

decision: The next 17 games project to about six wins, not a recovery pace.
ev_analysis: Mets' season win rate (.323) x 17, about 5.5 wins.
why: The raw-record mean lands near six wins and the same 'not a recovery' call, without the opponent conditioning or run-differential talent estimate.

decision: A variance-respecting composite ranks owners differently from championship counts.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: The decision is a ranking from a z-scored composite; group means do not rank individuals.

decision: Mets are slightly unlucky (22-24 Pythagorean vs 20-26) but on pace for ~76 wins, well short of 87.
ev_analysis: Their win-rate mean so far (.435) x 162, about 70 wins.
why: The record mean also says they fall short of the wild card, but cannot separate luck from skill.

decision: BaseRuns shows the Mets' run total is honest: a thin offense, not an unlucky one, so the ~76-win pace is real.
ev_analysis: Mets' runs per game vs league mean (23rd) carried forward.
why: Forecasting the current run mean forward gives the same 'thin offense' outlook, but never tests whether the runs were lucky.

decision: Honest preseason forecasts lock only clear gaps and call the rest coin flips.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: The framework is a game-by-game rule with a JND threshold and a standings projection; a group mean cannot express a coin-flip zone.

decision: Dipoto's 54% matches the AL WC3 cutoff (~88 wins), so it is a floor, not a target.
ev_analysis: Mean AL WC3 cutoff, 88.3 wins (54.5%); playoff rate of 87-88-win teams.
why: The decision is a group mean of cutoffs, which the analyst computes directly.

decision: Tanking perfectly does not buy the top pick; the lottery randomizes the prize.
ev_analysis: Share of worst-record NHL teams that won the lottery (mean of a 0/1).
why: The point is a base rate that the worst team usually does not win the lottery, which a group mean of outcomes gives.

decision: Even a record-worst NBA team usually misses the prize; the lottery denies it.
ev_analysis: Share of worst-record NBA teams that won the No. 1 pick.
why: A group base rate of worst teams winning the lottery delivers the same lesson.

decision: Two 16-3 champions in one week is surprising (about 1 in 470 years) but not destiny.
ev_analysis: Share of NBA champions at 16-3 (2/24) and NHL (1/39), multiplied.
why: The issue's base rate is two group proportions, which the analyst has.

decision: Peer enforcement in college sports is costly and likely to fail without repeat play.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A game-theory argument with no data; a group mean has nothing to estimate.

decision: The Mets' lineup is top-heavy mediocrity: Soto alone, with the floor at fault.
ev_analysis: Team mean OPS by club; Mets below the median.
why: The issue's point is the within-team spread; a mean alone reads as a uniformly mediocre lineup and loses the one-star shape.

decision: Caitlin Clark's closest statistical twin among NBA legends is Oscar Robertson.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Nearest-neighbor distance matching has no group-mean analogue.

decision: Hosts reach the semis 59% of the time, but the edge has faded and no host has won since 1998.
ev_analysis: Host semifinal rate 13/22 = 59%, with an era factor (recent vs older hosts) as cell means.
why: The decision is a group base rate with an era split, both available as cell means.

decision: The nearest analog to 2026 MLB is 2021; all five nearest are from 2017 on.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Nearest-neighbor matching in standardized feature space cannot be posed with group means.

decision: The 2026 Mets' statistical twin is the 2012 Mariners; outcomes diverge with strategy.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: An analog search, not a group comparison or base rate.

decision: The Astros' five nearest analogs were all closing windows; none won within five years.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: The comparison set is built by nearest-neighbor distance, which the analyst cannot form.

decision: Notre Dame will win the 2026 title, despite the checklist saying only 'contender'.
ev_analysis: Title rate of teams with top returning production and contender profile (a low base rate).
why: The group base rate says 'contender, stay calm', which is the checklist the issue explicitly overrides.

decision: With the three-point line added, Clark has no twin; she combines Robertson and Curry.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A distance-matching result; group means cannot find or dissolve a twin.

decision: Deadline buyers will overpay (winner's curse) for a prize worth about two wins.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: The winner's curse is about the maximum of many bids, a tail the analyst cannot pose; no bid data exist for a mean.

decision: Only five teams pass both the talent and maturity doors; they are the real title threats.
ev_analysis: Title rate by 2x2 cell (blue-chip gate x returning production) as cell means.
why: The tiered board is a two-factor sort, and factorial cell means deliver the same short list.

decision: Coin-flip contender games (like a 1.5-point line) are the most valuable on the schedule.
ev_analysis: Win rate of 1.5-point favorites (about a coin flip) as the forecast.
why: The base rate shows these games cannot be called, but their value as information (entropy) is beyond the tool.

decision: A strict 1-to-138 QB ranking from anonymous raters is unreliable and context-bound.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A critique of rater reliability and ranking; no group mean addresses it.

decision: Fantasy matchups are decided by the high-variance slots, not the highest-scoring player.
ev_analysis: Mean weekly points by position (QB ~17, RB ~7).
why: Means point to the QB as most important, the opposite of the issue's variance argument.

decision: Early-stabilizing numbers (velocity, K rate) warn of decline long before ERA does.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Which stats are trustworthy at what sample size is a reliability question, not a group mean.

decision: Selling Skubal cost Detroit about one point of title odds.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A with-and-without season simulation; no self-formed groups give the counterfactual.

decision: A 71% season-long favorite is only about a 52% bet in one sudden-death moment, so the worst losses share a shape.
ev_analysis: The favorite's per-game win rate, used as its chance in the big game.
why: A group mean says the edge is the same in every game, the opposite of the issue's claim that the summit shrinks it.

decision: Inviting all 365 teams with double elimination means fewer games and a fairer title (55% vs 45%).
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A simulation of a format that has never existed; no past group to average.

decision: Expansion to 76 raises the 12-over-5 upset rate about five points, and it would take ~300 years to detect.
ev_analysis: Historical 12-5 upset rate (~1 in 3) as the 2027 forecast.
why: The old-bracket group mean is exactly the base rate the issue says expires.

decision: A 29% season-long underdog is about 48% in one sudden-death game, which is why upsets feel so good.
ev_analysis: The underdog's per-game win rate used as its chance in one game.
why: The group mean keeps the underdog at its season rate, losing the narrowing the issue is about.

decision: A point spread is a calibrated probability: -7 wins about 70 of 100.
ev_analysis: Win rate of 7-point favorites in past games.
why: An empirical group base rate by spread delivers the same reading.

decision: A prediction-market price is a probability (38 cents = 38%).
ev_analysis: Share of contracts priced near 38 cents that paid out.
why: Calibration of price to outcome is a group base rate.

decision: A hot streak is worth most mid-season, little in April and nothing in August.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Requires simulating playoff odds with a forced streak at different dates.

decision: Tampa Bay is the division's third-best team by runs yet will win it; a six-game lead takes 131 games to erase.
ev_analysis: Each club's record win rate carried forward; Tampa's .594 keeps it ahead.
why: The record mean predicts Tampa wins the division, but because it reads them as the best team, which is the issue's very error.

decision: The Athletics, not the Mets, can move the most playoff probability as a spoiler.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Leverage is conditioning inside a season simulation; no group mean exists.

decision: Only the Philadelphia series matters for the Mets; sweeping it outweighs the rest.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A forced-sweep season simulation; group means cannot rank series by leverage.

decision: Flipping a team takes about four stars in baseball and one in basketball.
ev_analysis: Mean WAR of an All-Star (~4-5) vs the mean win gap between mediocre and contending teams (~12).
why: The baseball answer is group-mean arithmetic; the other sports are structural and the same for either analyst.

decision: Trading prospects for help now is usually sane; most 19-year-olds stay unknown, and the famous busts are survivors.
ev_analysis: Share of traded young prospects who became stars (a low base rate).
why: The decision rests on a base rate of prospect failure, which a group mean of outcomes gives.

decision: Oregon's rank is contested (5th to 76th); ask for the spread, not the ranking.
ev_analysis: Mean rank across systems, about the consensus 19th.
why: The mean is the consensus number the issue says hides the disagreement.

decision: A blowout says more about the loser; blowout winners do no better against the next line (47.9%).
ev_analysis: Cover rate next week for teams that beat the line by 20+ (47.9%).
why: The base rate gives 'no carryover', but by reading p >= .05 as no effect, and the rating-shift finding is beyond it.

decision: A losing-record division winner is likely (about 70%) this year, the first ever.
ev_analysis: Each club's .497 win rate x 3 games, so both finish about 80-82 and the winner has a losing record.
why: The point estimate says a sub-.500 champion, but as a certainty, not a 70% chance.

decision: Price a season by its area of hope: the Cubs banked 126 hope-days, the Mets one.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Needs daily simulated playoff probabilities; a group mean cannot produce them.

decision: A lottery ticket buys almost nothing; the state's take is exactly what players lose.
ev_analysis: Mean payout per dollar wagered across draws.
why: The decision is an expected value per ticket, which a group mean gives.

decision: An 80.3% make rate from 43 yards describes a crowd of kicks, not this one.
ev_analysis: Make rate from 43 yards (80.3%) as the forecast for Parkey's kick; clutch vs not, p = .052, read as no difference.
why: The analyst forecasts 80% but treats it as a property of the kick, the very reading the issue corrects.

decision: A 24% underdog winning is what a calibrated forecast expects about one time in four.
ev_analysis: Win rate of teams priced at about 24%.
why: Calibration is a group base rate.

decision: Our gloomiest Mets forecast was the most accurate, and the interval survived when the points did not.
ev_analysis: Mean error of the five point forecasts against 74 wins.
why: The analyst sees the gloomy forecast was closest but cannot see the interval, which is the issue's lesson.

decision: Bills and ND are the likeliest champions yet each wins only about 15-16 in 100.
ev_analysis: Title rate of past preseason or midseason favorites (a minority).
why: A favorites' base rate shows the favorite usually loses, but not the specific odds or the joint 1-in-40.

decision: Navy beats the spread two times in three but rarely wins (about 1 in 21).
ev_analysis: Win and cover rates of big underdogs and of academies as big underdogs.
why: Every number is a group base rate.

decision: Questionable players play about two in three times.
ev_analysis: Share of questionable players who played (9,634 / 14,346).
why: The codebook's model case: a group mean of a 0/1.

decision: The Bears traded later seasons for sooner ones: ~7 starter seasons in picks vs ~2.5 from Simmons.
ev_analysis: Mean starter seasons for comparable DTs aged 29-32 and for picks 17-32.
why: Both sides are group means.

decision: Outliving Woody Johnson is likely, but the Jets leaving the family is still worse than even odds.
ev_analysis: Share of teams sold after an owner's death (10/28, 36%).
why: The base rate lands at under even, but the analyst skips the lifetime (time-to-event) part and the range.

decision: Georgia is the likeliest champion at about 28% (range 6-60); below it the field is coin flips.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A bracket simulation with rating uncertainty and pairwise odds; a group mean cannot rank No. 2 against No. 11.

decision: An MLB lockout is likely (about 5 in 6), lost regular-season games about 1 in 3.
ev_analysis: Stoppage rate in new-system fights (10/12) and games-lost rate (7/12, 58%).
why: The stoppage mean matches, but the games-lost mean nearly doubles the issue's duration-based 1-in-3.

decision: Expect a shutout about 5-6 games in 100; Poisson fits goals except where hockey bends it.
ev_analysis: Share of team-games with zero goals (5.6 per 100).
why: The empirical mean gives the shutout rate, but without the Poisson curve the analyst cannot see where hockey departs from it.
